question.prompt:
In circle \(O\) chord \(\overline{AB}\) is produced so that \(\overline{BC}\) equals a radius of the circle. \(\overline{CO}\) is drawn and extended to \(D.\) \(\overline{AO}\) is drawn. Which of the following expresses the relationship between angles \(x\) and \(y?\)

[Figure 1](figures/1955_AMC_12_Q44_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The figure marks \(x=\angle AOD\) and \(y=\angle ACO\). Draw radius \(OB\). This creates two useful isosceles triangles: \(OB=BC\) by the given condition, and \(OA=OB\) because both are radii.

In triangle \(OBC\), the angles opposite the equal sides are equal. Since rays \(CA\) and \(CB\) coincide,
\[
\angle BOC=\angle BCO=y.
\]
Points \(A,B,C\) lie on a line in that order, so \(\angle ABO\) is an exterior angle of triangle \(OBC\). Thus
\[
\angle ABO=\angle BOC+\angle BCO=2y.
\]
Triangle \(OAB\) is isosceles, so \(\angle OAB=\angle ABO=2y\). Rays \(AB\) and \(AC\) coincide, giving \(\angle OAC=2y\).

Finally, \(C,O,D\) lie on a line in that order, so \(x\) is an exterior angle of triangle \(AOC\). Therefore
\[
x=\angle OAC+\angle ACO=2y+y=3y.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{x=3y}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Two isosceles triangles and exterior angles
